svg.text: T2 CLUSTER UNIT — 30,000 L SHARED FERROCEMENT TANK
Serves 10 households / 60 people, fed by 160 m² of aggregated roofs. Plan 1:100, section 1:50.
4 × Ø50 downpipes discharge into a common manifold
RCC ring beam 300 × 400 with 2 × Ø12 continuous
calmed inlet on a common manifold
sump: base falls 1% to a lockable 75 mm drain valve
1. Water is a common resource; the management rules matter as
much as the concrete. A WASH committee of 7 (≥ 4 women) is
formed before construction begins, not after.
2. Two caretakers are trained and paid a small stipend from a
water tariff of about 20–30 BDT per household per month.
3. The potable point is locked. The caretaker opens it morning
and evening; this protects the treated water and the filter
4. Conflict rule agreed in writing at handover: queue order,
priority for pregnant women, elderly and children, and a
penalty for washing clothes at the drinking tap.
5. Tank is cleaned twice a year (before and after monsoon) by
two trained people, never one alone, with the ladder and
a rope. Confined-space entry without a second person has
6. Chlorine is stored locked, away from children, in a labelled
opaque container. Dosing chart is fixed inside the lid.
7. Test the tank water for E. coli three times a year. Record
it on the board next to the tapstand where everyone sees it.
